item.title: Bobby Durkin hits game-winner to beat Cincinnati 63-61
item.description: CINCINNATI, OH - NOVEMBER 09: Minnesota Golden Gophers forward Bobby Durkin (3) reacts with his teammates after making a game-winning three-pointer during the game against the Minnesota Golden Gophers and the Cincinnati Bearcats on November 9, 2026 at Fifth Third Arena in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After trailing for most of the second half, the Gophers scrambled to come back and Bobby Durkin hit a deep three in the final seconds to beat the Cincinnati Bearcats 63-61 and remain undefeated. Kyan Evans did most of the work throughout the game, scoring 26 points, grabbing 10 rebounds and five assists. But it was Isaac Asuma, advancing the ball to Bobby Durkin, who hit his only three of the game to give Minnesota the lead with 0.4 on the clock and essentially sealing the win for Minnesota. Minnesota jumped out to an early lead and seemed to be controlling the game for the first 10 minutes of the game. But then Cincinnati just slowly took control of the pace of the game, playing good defense and making things difficult for everyone on the Gopher offense except Evans. The Bearcats forced a ton of Gopher turnovers that they turned into points, but Minnesota battled back and Durkin put the nail in the coffin to push the Gophers to 3-0 on the young season. WHY IT MATTERED: The win is great, being 3-0 is great, but this will count as a Quad 1 win for the Gophers and is the best non-conference win since beating North Carolina and West Virginia in back-to-back games in 2011. This is a game that will benefit the Gophers as they try to get back to the NCAA Tournament. GAME BALL: Evans had a double-double and his first big night scoring as a Gopher. But how do you not give the game ball to Bobby Buckets? THE STAT : For Cincinnati, it was turnovers; for the Gophers, it was offensive rebounds. Both were garnering extra possessions for their team and frustrating their fans. Cincy forced 17 turnovers that resulted in 16 points. Minnesota grabbed 13 offensive rebounds that allowed them to score 11 bonus points. TURNING POINT : This one was definitely in favor of the Bearcats, with a 79% chance of winning with 17 seconds left. And then MJ Collins missed the front end of a 1-and-1 and Asuma found Durkin for the game-winner. HOT : Cincinnati’s Tylen Riley has scored 11 points this season, but he was on fire tonight. The senior guard was 8/17 and 6/9 from three to finish with 25 points. NOT : Durkin had just two points and was 0-5 from three this game before he hit the game-winner. He had two threes blocked and looked out-of-sorts for most of this game. UP NEXT: The Gophers get a couple of gimme-games with Southern and Western Illinois coming to the Barn before three straight games against Power 5 teams. Southern is on Thursday at 7:00.

item.title: Purdue Uses a 21-2 Run to Blow By Illinois State: 76-59
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE, IN - NOVEMBER 09: Purdue Boilermakers guard Antione West Jr. (1) looks to pass while defined by Illinois State Redbirds guard Mason Klabo (3) in the first half of play during a men's college basketball game between the Illinois State Redbirds vs the Purdue Boilermakers on November 09, 2026 at Mackey Arena in West Lafayette, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Purdue came into this game looking to avoid their first 0-3 start since the 1950-1951 season. A season in which they finished 8-14 and 4-10 in conference play. Standing in their way was an Illinois State team from The Valley. Purdue changes up the starting lineup as you would expect with Antione West Jr. and Jack Benter being slotted in place of Omer Mayer and Gicarri Harris. The writing was on the wall with that one given the substitution pattern you saw in the two overtimes from the game against Valparaiso. John Wooden Memorial Player of the Game (JWMPOTG): Giving this one to Antione West Jr. in what I hope is his coming out party. The redshirt freshman went 7-11 from the floor including 3-4 from three and helped spark the run that put this game out of reach. Purdue needed to do a number of things to return a little bit of hope to the fanbase. First and foremost they needed to win. That’s always number one. Second though, they needed to shoot the ball better, show better effort on defense, and maybe, just maybe, play a full 40 minutes. If Buddy the Elf can recharge in just 40 minutes there’s no reason that this Purdue men’s basketball team can’t play a good 40 minutes of basketball. While Purdue looked better in the first half than they did the last 30 minutes we saw them play, the second half and double overtime against Valparaiso, they still had plenty of problems. Purdue’s offense too often resulted in clumps of players around the perimeter just sort of standing there. That’s no way to run an offense. Purdue was also incredibly streaky in the first half. At one point they hit seven shots in a row. Then, toward the end of the half they went 1-9. I won’t say it was feast or famine because what we watched was no feast. Purdue did shoot the three better in the first half but that might be partly because they shot far fewer. In the first half they went 4/10 from three. West hit two threes while Benter and Jacobsen added one a piece. Yes, Jacobsen. He was again Purdue’s leading scorer heading into halftime as the only Boilermaker in double figures with 10. On defense the Boilermakers did a good job handling the Redbirds three point shooting. They came into this game shooting just over 50% from three in their first two games. In the first half of this one Purdue held them to 3-16 from three with one of those made threes being a bank in off the glass. Despite these good numbers on defense Illinois State continued to chip away at the lead. Purdue never looked comfortable out there and went into half with a smaller lead

item.title: Finally, Purdue basketball finds its offense late to run off Illinois State
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − At last, Purdue basketball fans can breathe a sigh of relief. It took huge late run to blow the game open, but the Boilermakers left Mackey Arena with their first victory. A lineup change that included Jack Benter and Antione West Jr. among the starting helped pilot Purdue 's 76-59 win over Illinois State . Purdue (1-2) led 50-48 midway through the second half before landing the knockout blow it needed after losses to Gonzaga and Valparaiso to open the season while also snapping out of its 3-point shooting funk. After combining to shoot just 20.4% from 3 in the first two games, the Boilers made 8 of 19 against the Redbirds (1-2). Purdue basketball turning point vs. Illinois State Despite a hot shooting first half, Purdue couldn't separate itself from the Redbirds. Illinois State had a chance to cut the lead to two Louie Semona II's 3-pointer was off and Enzo Shahrvin pulled down the rebound. Purdue called timeout to set up a final play. Antione West Jr. ended up making a stepback 3-pointer from the right wing to give the Boilermakers a 36-28 halftime lead. That shot was Purdue's saving grace for a long time, but it was just enough to keep Illinois State from ever pulling even or going ahead. Eventually, Purdue found its footing and blew the game open with a 24-2 run relying on a lineup of Antione West Jr., Luke Ertel, CJ Cox, Jack Benter and Daniel Jacobsen. Game MVP Jack Benter received his first two career starts out of necessity when Trey Kaufman-Renn was sidelined to open last season. On Monday, the junior was in the starting rotation for the first time in a year. He showed what he's capable of from the get go, sinking a 3-pointer for the game's first points, then drawing a charge on the defensive end. It set the stage for a productive night across the board for Benter, who finished with 14 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists and a steal. 3 Purdue basketball standouts vs. Illinois State Daniel Jacobsen: Three games in a row is a trend. The 7-foot-4 center is Purdue's best offensive piece. It was another stellar night for the Boilermaker big man, contributing his third straight game with at least 20 points, hitting that number on the nose. Jacobsen also had 7 rebounds and 3 assists. Antione West Jr.: In his first career start after sitting out last season, West had a coming out party. West scored 17 points on 7 of 11 shooting and added 2 rebounds, 2 assists and a steal. CJ Cox: The junior guard made three early midrange jumpers. He didn't fill up the stat sheet, but he didn't hurt the Boilermakers either. Cox had 10 points, 3 assists and, in typical Cox fashion, no turnovers. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. For the unversed, the President had taken to his Truth Social account to announce that the UFC CEO and several other fighters were welcome to join his cabinet. However, just a day after the announcement, Trump clarified that the offer was made in a jovial spirit and that he was only joking. While he maintained that White would be a fantastic choice for the position, he insisted that there was nothing serious behind the proposal. The UFC CEO had confirmed that he would meet Trump on November 9 after returning to the United States from the Zuffa Boxing 12 event in London. However, the President later clarified that White’s visit had nothing to do with the press secretary offer. According to Trump, the UFC boss was already planning to be in Washington and had simply decided to stop by and see him. And that is exactly what White ended up doing. During the November 9 White House news conference alongside Trump, White officially turned down the prospect of becoming press secretary. While admitting that he doesn’t say no to the President, the UFC CEO made it clear that he had no interest in entering politics at the moment. He said, “I don’t tell the president no to anything. item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect President Donald Trump has been pushing for a Pete Rose pardon for more than a year now. And on Monday, he made it clear that he still hasn’t given up on the idea. During a White House press briefing alongside UFC CEO Dana White, Trump said that he “would give Pete Rose a pardon” for the tax charges that the late MLB hits leader pleaded guilty to in 1990. Trump also insisted that the former Cincinnati Reds star had been “very mistreated” by baseball and said that Rose deserved to be in the Hall of Fame “a long time ago.” Pete Rose’s Long Saga Rose finished his career with 4,256 hits, the most in MLB history. But he was banned from baseball in 1989 after an investigation found that he had bet on games, including Reds games, while managing the team. A year later, Rose pleaded guilty to two felony counts of filing false federal income tax returns after underreporting more than $300,000 in income from appearances, autograph sessions, memorabilia sales, and gambling winnings. He served five months in federal prison. Rose’s lifetime ban kept him off the Hall of Fame ballot for decades, and his requests to be reinstated were repeatedly denied, as was his request for the Hall to reconsider . He died in September 2024 at the age of 83. In March 2025, Trump announced on Truth Social that he would be “signing a complete pardon” for Rose. Two months later, commissioner Rob Manfred removed Rose from MLB’s permanently ineligible list, though his earliest chance at the Hall of Fame is the Classic Baseball Era Committee ballot in December 2027, per ESPN . ’40 years of hell’ On Monday, White was at the White House taking questions from reporters after Trump claimed he was “only kidding” about making him press secretary. item.title: 3 notes from Indiana women’s basketball’s 84-56 win over Bradley
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - NOVEMBER 03: Indiana Hoosiers head coach Teri Moren with the high five in the second half of play during a women's college basketball game between Florida Gulf Coast Eagles vs the Indiana Hoosiers on November 03, 2026 at Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana women’s basketball beat Bradley 84-56 on Monday night at Assembly Hall in Bloomington. The win brings the Hoosiers to 3-0 on the season with a few more matchups to come before they face their first real test against Mississippi State toward the end of the month. All three have given Indiana things to feel good about, and Monday’s win was no different. Here’s a few observations: Taking control in the second quarter Indiana actually entered the second quarter with an 18-15 deficit. The Hoosiers shot poorly from all over the court while the Braves did enough on the interior to pull ahead. Bradley’s an interesting team to go against, as Teri Moren explained after the game. The Braves run a ton of movement on offense and Moren was eager to see how her roster responded to such a different challenge after two dominant wins to open the season. The Hoosiers responded alright, winning the second quarter 27-8 while dominating the glass to surge ahead for a lead they’d never relinquish. Malia Samuels was vital, going 4-4 from the field while pulling down a pair of rebounds and logging an assist. Indiana’s been capable of really hitting the gas under Moren and this team is showing it can have that gear early on. Maya Makalusky making an impact Makalusky, a second-year forward, performed well all over the court in leading Indiana with 16 points on the night. She finished shooting 4-6 from 3-point range while tying for second on the team in rebounding with five. Indiana’s going to need more nights like this from Makalusky, who committed years ago as the top prospect in the state. Her overall skillset fits well into what Moren likes to do on both ends of the floor, so it’s all about developing into that role. Lenee Beaumont Indiana was without Lenee Beaumont, its on-court leader, who left the game in the second quarter after seeming to tweak something in her leg after getting into the paint. She remained on the bench with the team, however. The Los Angeles Lakers have gotten off to such a hot start in the 2026-27 season, and that’s thanks in large part to the heater Luka Doncic has been on all season long to this point. Doncic entered play on Monday against the Atlanta Hawks with a league-leading average of 40.1 points per game — scoring at a rate that’s simply unprecedented, even amongst the most elite bucket-getters in the history of the NBA. The Lakers, with Doncic going on a scoring binge, have won nine of their first 11 games, and Doncic has even missed two of those games — both Purple and Gold victories. Not everybody may be a fan of Doncic’s heliocentric style of play and overall dominance of the basketball, but head coach JJ Redick knows that giving the ball to the 27-year-old superstar is a surefire recipe for success. In fact, Redick mentioned that Doncic’s motivation to score as many points as possible comes from his burning desire to lead the Lakers to as many victories as he can. item.title: Jacksonville Jaguars Become A Super Bowl Favorite After Trades
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 05: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars celebrates a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens during the fourth quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 05, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty A shocking day of trades saw the Jacksonville Jaguars boost their chances of winning the Super Bowl by acquiring better defenders. Jacksonville made three noteworthy trades on Monday to land Davon Godchaux, Jessie Bates III, and Jordan Davis to show their confidence. The Jaguars clearly made these moves due to believing in their core having a chance to win the franchise’s first Super Bowl victory. Most odds sites have seen Jacksonville rise in the Super Bowl favorites, with Fanduel having the following odds: San Francisco 49ers: +550 Buffalo Bills: +600 Jaguars: +750 Chicago Bears : +850 Kansas City Chiefs : +1200 Los Angeles Rams : +1300 The season started with the Rams as the Super Bowl favorites before losses and injuries harmed their chances. Trevor Lawrence has led the Jaguars to become one of the top AFC teams with strong games every week. Jacksonville could be undefeated with the only two losses coming in close games. Adding three defenders should improve the team’s overall defense with more talent on the roster. The Jaguars currently hold a three-game lead over the Houston Texans for the top of the AFC South. A playoff spot seems nearly guaranteed, but more moves were needed to have a stronger chance at winning the Super Bowl. Comparing Jacksonville Jaguars To Other Contenders Current odds show the Bills, Jaguars, and 49ers all within each other as the forecasted best three teams come playoff time. Josh Allen is still leading Buffalo, and the franchise has come close for many years as a top AFC East team. Most pressure is on the Bills for getting closer to the goal but failing to reach it. The 49ers made a Super Bowl appearance just a few seasons ago with the dynamic offense led by Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey. San Francisco and Buffalo both have more high-level playoff experience on their side than Jacksonville. However, that’s why the Jaguars decided to make trades and treat this season as one they are going “all in” on. The three new defenders, young rising star Travis Hunter, and other consistent players could make them one of the best defenses in the league. Lawrence must continue playing strong to lead the offense since a lot of pressure falls on him. What Jacksonville Jaguars Super Bowl Would Mean Jacksonville fans feel the need for a Super Bowl as much as any other fan base in the league. The Jaguars have never played in a Super Bowl game and have a heartbreaking 0-3 record in AFC Championship games throughout their franchise history. Many are arguing this is owner Shad Khan’s best chance to finally bring a Super Bowl to Jacksonville. Johnson is the league's third-oldest active quarterback behind the Steelers' Aaron Rodgers and Bengals backup Joe Flacco . item.title: Vikings Announce Move on Odell Beckham Jr. Hours Before Bills Game
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 24: Odell Beckham Jr. #3 of the Miami Dolphins warms up prior to the game against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium on November 24, 2024 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) Getty The Buffalo Bills will face a longtime veteran wide receiver when they take the field against the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. The Vikings announced hours before the game that they were signing veteran Odell Beckham Jr. to their active roster. The Vikings had added Beckham to the practice squad, but had yet to elevate him to the active roster for a game. Odell Beckham Jr. Set to Face Bills As reporter Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk noted, there had been rumors over the weekend that the Vikings planned to sign Beckham to their active roster. “Word that the Vikings would sign Beckham to their 53-man roster surfaced on Sunday and the team announced the move on Monday afternoon,” Alper reported. “Beckham has been on the practice squad for the last couple of weeks and was elevated to the active roster once without appearing in a game.” Beckham appeared in three games for the New York Giants , but was released without making a catch, Alper noted. “[Beckham] did not play in 2025, so he’ll be looking for his first regular season catch since he was with the Dolphins in Week 14 of the 2024 season,” Alper added. Beckham was not among the inactives for Monday’s game, giving him a chance to continue his NFL comeback. Bills Had Shot at Odell Beckham More Than a Decade Ago The Bills famously had a chance to land Odell Beckham Jr., who came into the NFL as a first-round pick of the New York Giants in 2014. The Bills were desperate for help on offense going into that draft and moved up to the No. 4 overall pick, where they landed Sammy Watkins. Though Watkins had flashes of strong play throughout his career, he also dealt with several injuries and stayed in Buffalo only three seasons before being traded to the Los Angeles Rams in 2017. The 2014 draft class was seen as one of the best wide receiver crops in years, and the Bills also lost out on a chance to land Mike Evans, who was taken later in the first round by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . item.title: Josh Allen has run for 5,000 yards and only 4 other QBs can say that
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball for a first down against the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Josh Allen has run for 5,000 yards in the NFL. For a guy whose primary job is throwing the football, that’s a lot of ground covered. The Buffalo Bills quarterback became just the fifth quarterback in NFL history to reach that total during Buffalo’s Week 9 game against the Minnesota Vikings. Allen crossed the 5k mark in the third quarter on a series of designed runs. He entered the game at 4991 then had a 7-yard run in the first quarter to get to 4998. He lost one yard on the kneel down to end the first half to fall back to 4997. A 5-yard scramble from the Minnesota 21 was followed by a 3-yard run to make sure he was over. And counting… Allen joins Lamar Jackson, Michael Vick, Cam Newton, and Russell Wilson in the 5,000-yard group. That’s the entire list, and Allen has put himself on it in his ninth NFL season. Bills fans have watched those yards come a few different ways. There have been scrambles after the protection breaks down, designed runs, and more than a few plays where Allen decides the best way to get a first down is to go through whoever is standing in front of him. They all count. Of course, if he slid more often, like we all keep screaming for him to do, it would have taken a few more carries to get there. Allen already owns the NFL record for career rushing touchdowns by a quarterback. Now he has another number to go with it, and another reminder of how much of Buffalo’s offense has come from his legs.

item.title: Ilia Topuria Confident Arman Tsarukyan Would ‘Panic’ Against Him
item.description: Ilia Topuria Arman Tsarukyan Getty Former UFC lightweight champion Ilia Topuria said that he is confident he would make Arman Tsarukyan “panic” against him in a fight. Topuria is set to return to the Octagon in early 2027, and while a matchup against rival Paddy Pimblett seems likely, it’s also possible that he could fight Tsarukyan in what would truly be an incredible fight between two of the most well-rounded lightweights in the sport. If the fight does happen, then Topuria is confident he would defeat Tsarukyan. Ilia Topuria Speaks About Potential Arman Tsarukyan Fight Speaking to ABC MMA, Topuria shared his thoughts on a potential lightweight bout against Tsarukyan, predicting it would go like Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev. “Arman would be pure panic on the feet trying to take you down. Like Movsar against Volk, the same thing. They are used to dominating all the time, and their confidence grows through that domination. When you cannot dominate, especially as a wrestler, wrestling and takedown defense in MMA have evolved so much that without good ground skills alongside your wrestling, it becomes exhausting. Arman does not stand out for his ground game,” Topuria said (via MMAJunkie.com ). “He stands out for takedowns and the dominant positions he looks for. How often have you seen someone stop those takedowns and go after him? Like what happened against Volk. He (Evloev) was so used to taking people down, resting in the clinch or on their backs, but with Volk, he could not do any of that. What happened? Panic, and he gave up. I have been world champion in two divisions, in four world title fights. … I grew up grappling and wrestling. I have more wrestling photos than photos playing in the park. It’s my life.” Will Ilia Topuria Fight Arman Tsarukyan in 2027? MMA fans would surely love to see Topuria fight Tsarukyan in 2027, as it would be one of the highest-level bouts that the promotion could put together next year. However, it feels like right now it will be Justin Gaethje vs. Tsarukyan and Topuria vs. Pimblett first, with the winners of those bouts fighting each other. item.title: Josh Johnson leaving Bengals practice squad to join Arizona Cardinals
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals practice squad quarterback Josh Johnson is being signed to the Arizona Cardinals’ 53-man roster, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. This comes as the Cardinals’ quarterback room has been completely flipped upside down. They started with Jacoby Brissett, who was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. They then turned to Gardner Minshew, who unfortunately went down with a likely season-ending torn UCL. Now, they’ll sign Johnson, who started the year off with the Bengals, was eventually cut, and was then re-signed to the practice squad. With veteran QB Gardner Minshew sidelined due to a UCL injury, the Cardinals are signing QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals’ practice squad, per sources. The Cardinals will be Johnson’s 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons. pic.twitter.com/5ZIN2IpZRQ — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 10, 2026 Despite being 40 years old, Johnson performed actually rather well for the Bengals in the preseason. He actually made it a bit of a debate for some on whether or not to keep him as a third QB, though the Bengals opted to get him onto the practice squad along with Sean Clifford, the latter of whom is now essentially QB3 in Cincinnati. Johnson will now be the NFL’s second-oldest starting quarterback, behind the Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers, whom the Bengals will face this week on Sunday Night Football. Unfortunately for Johnson, he’s already lost his No. 1 target, Michael Wilson, who suffered a neck injury in Week 9 and will miss the rest of the season. With Wilson out, tight end Trey McBride will likely see even more targets, despite already being the team’s leading pass catcher.
